messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error in R-INLA ZeroInflated models
parts:
Hi,

I don't know what "zeroinflatednbinomial2" is, but I can give you some general advice.

1. You can try a different initial value for the hyper-parameters
2. You can delete the 0s from your dataset and fit a truncated nbinomial
3. You can do simulation-inference with your model, and see whether the parameters can be recovered or not (with your model and data size)

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error in R-INLA ZeroInflated models
parts:
yes, seems like you run into problems here. there is no much info about
in almost-only zeros.

I would suggest to simulate some data with known structure and then you
can see how much zeros your model can take.

H
